plan: Final integrated experiment design as a single consolidated document with sections (i)–(x). (i) Restated the question as multi-objective with Pareto-front + hypervolume framing and a primary composite scalar (geometric mean over {p-logP improvement, QED improvement, 1−hallucination-rate, scaffold-diversity preservation}). (ii) Adopted defaults A1–A7 and unknowns B1–B8 with a one-line reversal note per unknown. (iii) Six arms A0/A1/A2/A3/A4/A_minus with an explicit 'embedding?' column; headline contrast pre-registered as {A2,A3,A4} vs. A0, with A1 as matched-compute post-hoc reference and A_minus as chemistry-blind placebo. (iv) Data plan: MOSES ZINC, ChEMBL-target slice (disjoint), scaffold-split surrogate, inchi-key leakage controls, locked MOSES scaffold-test as primary eval set. (v) Per-arm feedback integration with granularity: per-sample RL (A2), per-token decoding guidance (A3), per-round DAA-style retraining (A4), with composite-reweighting sweep and a secondary MM-style KL alignment metric. (vi) Pre-registered metric table with primary set {M1 composite, M2 hallucination index aggregated over 5 sub-signals including ultra-long C-path ≥8, heavy-atom 99th-pct, period-separated fragments, valence errors, repeated-symbol runs; M3 scaffold-diversity primary; M4 p-logP; M5 QED} and secondaries {internal Tanimoto, Morgan-FP MMD as FCD substitute, binding-proxy with decoy negative control, validity/uniqueness/novelty, Pareto/hypervolume}; null hypotheses stated per primary. (vii) Statistics: N=2000/seeds × k=3 seeds, paired bootstrap B=2000, Bonferroni α'=0.01 over 5 primaries, Cohen's d with bootstrap CI, sample-efficiency curves on both axes, decision rule pre-registered. (viii) Two compute tiers (1×GPU×1 wk; 24-CPU×48h RNN-only) and explicit statement of in-bubble infeasibility with a tested stdlib stub artifact in /workspace/_stub/. (ix) Risk register R1–R10. (x) Decision table O1–O8 mapping outcomes to conclusions about embedding chemical feedback, including placebo-tied and post-hoc-filter-tied failure modes.

context.question: Incorporating the chemical feedback mechanism, which leverages properties such as p-logP, QED, and binding affinity, directly improves the generation of molecules with superior chemical properties and reduces molecular hallucinations in targeted molecule discovery tasks. Does embedding this feedback loop better align molecule generation with real-world distributions, preserving structural diversity (e.g., avoiding over-representation of ultra-long carbon chains) while enhancing property scores?
context.context: Design an experiment that answers the question. The researcher can clarify source-supported setup details by topic. Do not claim that an experiment was run.
